newsitem.title: GREECE: Athens bourse climbs as construction rallies.
newsitem.headline: Athens bourse climbs as construction rallies.

text.p: Greek equities settled 0.64 percent higher on Wednesday on moderate volume with construction shares gaining 4.97 percent recovering from oversold levels, market watchers said.
They expected buying interest to continue to be limited in view of the Greek Orthodox Easter holidays.
The Greek bourse will be closed on Friday and Monday.

"The market is neutral in view of the Easter holidays. The general share index will continue to trade at current levels for the next couple of weeks," said analyst Vassilis Kletsas, at Telesis Securities.
Investors are awaiting the release of preliminary forecasts on such macroeconomic figures as inflation and state revenues, usually released at the end of the month, he added.

"The construction sector has underperformed up to now. Its stocks were oversold and because people are turning away from banks, we saw construction shares jump towards the end of the session," he said.

The Athens general share index ended 0.64 percent or 9.22 points higher on Wednesday, at 1,442.19, after opening at 1433.08. It had closed at 1,432.97 on Tuesday. The session's high was at 1,433.15 points.
Turnover was 14.0 billion drachmas on 4.5 million shares traded. Advancers led decliners 149 to 71, with 20 stocks unchanged on 240 traded.
There were block trades in Alpha Credit, Macedonia-Thrace Bank, Dias and Aluminium of Greece.
Sectoral indices were mixed. Constructrion shares led, climbing 4.97 percent. Banks rose a slight 0.11 percent and industrials gained 1.09 percent.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted at 1,081.0- 1,111.0. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, were flat at 6,150 drachmas.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $61.56-$63.26. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The ING Baring Financial Products American- style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted higher at 2,196-2,392 drachmas.
The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted lower at $13.07-N/O. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.
